item.title: Chip Brown sponsors legislation enforcing Alabama’s seafood labeling law
item.description: Interim House Majority Leader Chip Brown (R-Hollinger’s Island) announced on Monday that he has filed legislation that “further strengthens Alabama’s existing seafood labeling law and forces restaurants to comply with its provisions or face severe penalties.”Restaurants located in Alabama are currently required to disclose whether seafood is domestic or imported on the menu listing for dishes they sell or on conspicuous signage plainly visible to diners and patrons. item.title: Alabama House passes Sarah Marsh Heaven’s 27 Camp Safety Act
item.description: MONTGOMERY — The Alabama House passed a bill on Tuesday to establish safety plans for summer camps across the state.State Rep. David Faulkner (R-Mountain Brook) sponsored House Bill 381 (HB381).The safety measures include a required safety license from the Alabama Management Agency (AEMA) and developing emergency and evaluation plans. item.title: Senate committee holds public hearing on bill setting minimum police staffing requirements for Montgomery, other Class 3 cities
item.description: The Senate County and Municipal Government Committee held a public hearing on legislation setting staffing standards for law enforcement agencies in Montgomery and Huntsville.The bill by State Sen. Will Barfoot (R-Pike Road) would provide minimum staffing requirements for Class 3 municipal law enforcement agencies. Alabama has two Class 3 cities, Montgomery and Huntsville. item.title: Eighth-inning surge lifts Alabama baseball over Samford
item.description: In their first midweek matchup of the season, Alabama’s bats were nowhere to be found for most of the game. Eventually, the offense got going as the Crimson Tide escaped with a 3-2 road victory over Samford.For seven innings, the Alabama offense was held to just one hit, frustrating a lineup that put up big numbers against Washington State a few days ago. item.title: No. 9 Auburn baseball shut out in midweek loss to Cincinnati
item.description: No. 9 Auburn baseball faced an early deficit against Cincinnati on Tuesday night at Plainsman Park and was unable to muster any runs as it fell 8-0 in its first piece of midweek action. The story of the game for Auburn was a 0-for-9 mark at the plate with runners in scoring position and only five hits on the night, one game after the Tigers exploded for 20 hits in Game Three of its weekend series with Youngstown State.
